title: Fix intermittent scheduler livelock from cross-tenant preemption and KV cache churn
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent production degradations spanning Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Symptoms: sudden spike in 95/99th token latency and persistent backlog on a subset of workers for 30-90s followed by normal recovery. Investigation indicates a scheduler livelock where cross-tenant preemption logic repeatedly reshuffles waiting batches while aggressive KV-cache eviction / refetch churn causes repeated cold-KV requests that keep affected requests from making forward progress. This ticket tracks root-cause fix, short-term mitigations, testing, and rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a mixed workload with latency-sensitive short-turn requests and long-context streaming requests (2k+ tokens) from two tenant ids.
2) Configure autoscaler to allow burst preemption (Dedicated) and enable aggressive KV eviction (low-memory quantized models).
3) Create sustained microburst of short requests from tenant A while tenant B has in-flight long-context generation that performs KV refetches.

4) Observe scheduler repeatedly preempting queues to service perceived high-priority tenant A, while the long-context requests for tenant B keep missing cached KV and requeueing, producing 95/99 latency spikes and backlog that does not drain immediately.
observed_behavior: Repeated queue reshuffles and re-queueing of long-context batches; worker-level queues show a stable set of requests cycling without completion for tens of seconds; affected requests show repeated KV-cache misses and network fetches to storage layer.
expected_behavior: Scheduler should ensure fairness and forward progress: once a batch has been dispatched and started, it should make progress to completion even if preemption events occur elsewhere; KV-cache eviction should not cause repeated full refetch loops for in-flight contexts.
root_cause_summary: Intersecting logic bugs across three subsystems: (1) preemption heuristics treat in-flight batches as preemptable when they are mid-KV refetch, leading to repeated re-queues; (2) KV cache eviction policy lacks a 'in-flight pin' and can evict blocks that are still required by running requests; (3) the scheduler's fairness token bucket resets on certain requeue paths, allowing starvation amplification. The combination creates a livelock in which batches are unable to complete while new short requests continuously take precedence.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Turn off aggressive preemption for tiered customers and reduce preemption frequency in Hosted for 24 hours (hotfix config flag). 2) Add a conservative in-flight pin timeout to KV cache (30s) to prevent immediate eviction of blocks referenced by active requests. 3) Emergency throttling for new short-request bursters at edge gateway for affected tenants.
fix_summary: Implement a three-part permanent fix: A) Mark KV blocks referenced by in-flight sequences as 'pinned' until the batch completes or a safety timeout, preventing eviction-induced thrash. B) Modify scheduler preemption to detect in-flight KV refetch states and avoid preempting batches that have made non-trivial progress (e.g., >10% tokens generated or >1 KV refetch). C) Strengthen fairness accounting so requeue paths do not reset priority tokens; add unit tests and property tests for forward progress.
implementation_notes: - Scheduler changes in pkg/scheduler/preemption.go: add has_made_progress flag and preemption veto when true.
- KV cache changes in pkg/kv/cache.go: add in_flight_pin map keyed by request_id with expiry and metrics.
- Add e2e scenario harness in infra/tests/continuous_batching_livelock_test.go replicating mixed-tenant microbursts.
- Bench: run runtime perf job runtime-stability/livelock-24h on staging-2 and dedicated-canary.
- Note: Private deployments require opt-in config flag kv.in_flight_pin=true for initial rollout.
- Migration: small DB migration to add request_pin TTLs (idempotent).
qa_plan: - Unit tests: cover preemption veto and KV pin expiry edge cases.
- Integration: e2e harness reproducing 2k token long-context + short-request microburst; assert no 30s backlog with fix.
- Staging canary: deploy to staging-2, run 12h stress with 5 tenants and verify 99th token latency < 3x baseline.
- Dedicated canary: small cohort of Dedicated customers who opt-in; monitor for regressions for 48h.
- Private: provide patch bundle and test instructions to SEs; request customer regression window before enabling by default.
deployment_plan: - Phase 1: Apply config change to reduce preemption frequency in Hosted and enable KV in_flight_pin as opt-in in runtime-1.28. Roll out to 10% of hosts.
- Phase 2: Merge PR and roll to staging; run automated stress harness for 24h.
- Phase 3: Canary to Dedicated canaries (weekend low-traffic window), monitor for 48h, rollback criteria defined.
- Phase 4: Coordinate with Private deployments: publish patch, require customer upgrade during maintenance window.
- Rollback: revert config flags and redeploy previous runtime image if 99th latency increases > 2x baseline or error rates > 0.5%.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Add metric runtime.scheduler.requeues_per_request and alert if > 5 for a request over 10s window.
- Track runtime.kv.in_flight_pins and pin_evictions to detect pin thrash.
- Dashboard: Livelock triage board with per-tenant 95/99 token latency, KV miss rate, and queue depth heatmap.
- Pager rule: high severity if >3 customers hit >30s backlog in 10m window (paged to oncall).
- Create synthetic probe that simulates mixed-tenant microburst every 5 minutes in canary clusters.
postmortem_tasks: - Complete incident postmortem doc and link to-ticket: CONFLUENCE-RT-1024.
- Add long-running e2e test to CI to prevent regressions.
- Review autoscaler interaction with preemption heuristics in a follow-up RFC.
- Update runbooks for SEs and SREs describing emergency mitigations and private deployment upgrade steps.
